title: Equal homogeneous classes give a locally constant scalar coboundary
statement: Let $K$ be a field, $S$ its separable closure, $G=\mathrm{Gal}(S/K)$, and $z,w$ homogeneous continuous degree-two cocycles for the discrete units of $S$ [def-sc-galois-units-cohomology]. If their cohomology projections agree, there is a locally constant $a:G\to S^\times$ with $c_z(g,h)/c_w(g,h)=a(g)g(a(h))/a(gh)$ for all $g,h$, where $c_z,c_w$ are the homogeneous evaluations [def-sc-brauer-scalar-defect].

proof.text:
the homogeneous cohomology is the kernel of d2 modulo the image of d1.
Equality of the projections therefore supplies an invariant continuous homogeneous
one-cochain F whose differential is z-w. Evaluate at (1,g) and put a(g)=F(1,g).toMul.
The coefficient topology is discrete, so continuity makes a locally constant.
Homogeneous equivariance gives F(g,g*h)=g(F(1,h)), while the degree-one differential
at (1,g,g*h) is F(g,g*h)-F(1,g*h)+F(1,g). Translating this additive equality to units
gives c_z/c_w=a(g)*g(a(h))/a(g*h), with precisely the sign shown below.
No normalization of either representative is required.
